\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{رحم} (rahm)}{رحم (rahm)}]{\ur{رحم} (rahm) — mercy; pity}

\label{lesson:UR-C360-rahm}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for however, then the Urdu for to give in.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{رحم}}
\textbf{\ur{رحم}} — \emph{rahm} — \textquotedblleft{}mercy; pity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{جج} \ur{نے} \ur{ملزم} \ur{پر} \ur{رحم} \ur{کیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jaj ne mulzim par rahm kiyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The judge showed the accused mercy.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{رحم}} (\emph{rahm}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{raḥm}, \textquotedblleft{}tenderness, compassion\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rahm}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rahm}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jaj ne mulzim par rahm kiyā.} — The judge showed the accused mercy.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for however, then the Urdu for to give in, then say \emph{rahm} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تھامنا} (thāmnā)}{تھامنا (thāmnā)}]{\ur{تھامنا} (thāmnā) — to hold on to; to hold up}

\label{lesson:UR-C360-thamna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for loyal, then the Urdu for a sin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تھامنا}}
\textbf{\ur{تھامنا}} — \emph{thāmnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to hold on to; to hold up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{مشکل} \ur{وقت} \ur{میں} \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{میرا} \ur{ہاتھ} \ur{تھاما۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mushkil vaqt meṅ us ne merā hāth thāmā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In a hard time she held my hand.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{رسی} \ur{تھامی}, \emph{us ne rassī thāmī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تھامنا}} (\emph{thāmnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{thāmnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to prop, to stop\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{stámbhate} (CDIAL 13683).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}
